item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q003_actin_like_atpase_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, the catalytic domains are separate families within the same Actin-like ATPase domain superfamily c.55.1 (SUNID 53067): Actin/HSP70 is c.55.1.1 (SUNID 53068), hexokinase is c.55.1.3 (SUNID 53083), and glycerol kinase is c.55.1.4 (SUNID 53089). The superfamily belongs to the Ribonuclease H-like motif fold c.55 in the alpha/beta class. Sharing a superfamily—not merely a fold—supports remote homology and descent of their catalytic cores from a common ancestor, with conservation of an actin-like structural and nucleotide-coupling framework despite major functional divergence. It does not license transfer of substrate specificity, precise reaction, regulation, oligomeric state, cellular role, or full-length domain architecture. Cross-family structures may guide the conserved core only; family-specific templates and representatives are preferable for functional modeling because loops, insertions, boundaries, and active-site details can differ substantially.","evidence_used":["Tools used: mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info, mcp__scope__search_scop, mcp__scope__get_scop_node, mcp__scope__list_scop_children","mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53067/children?limit=100","mcp__scope__get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53067, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53067/parents, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53067/homology","mcp__scope__get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53068, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53068/parents","mcp__scope__get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53083, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53083/parents","mcp__scope__get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53089, /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53089/parents"]}]}
